title: PRESIDENT OF INDIA GRACES THE VALEDICTORY CEREMONY OF THE GOLDEN JUBILEE CELEBRATIONS OF THE VAIDYARATNAM AYURVEDA COLLEGE
subtitle: AYURVEDIC COLLEGES SHOULD SERVE THE COMMUNITY WITH AUTHENTIC AND EFFECTIVE AYURVEDA: PRESIDENT DROUPADI MURMU
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 2:37PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The President of India, Smt Droupadi Murmu graced the valedictory ceremony of the Golden Jubilee celebrations of the Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College at Thrissur, Keralam today (November 27, 2026).
Speaking on the occasion, the President said that Keralam’s contribution goes beyond enhancing the international reputation of Ayurveda. It has nurtured a rich and living tradition of classical Ayurvedic learning. It has also enriched the medical knowledge passed down through generations of Vaidya families. Its traditions of preparing authentic Ayurvedic medicines have continued to flourish unabated.
The President said that a remarkable feature of Ayurveda is that its authentic literature has never been limited to Sanskrit. In Keralam, a lot of original work and commentaries have been produced in Malayalam and Manipravalam also.
The President said that every Ayurvedic College should serve the community with authentic and effective Ayurveda. It should also impart topical Ayurvedic education. Such colleges should be able to create experts who have the wisdom to effectively respond to the health challenges of the present and future generations. She was happy to note that the work ethos of Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College is aligned with this dictum.
The President said that Ayurvedic institutions like Vaidyaratnam Ayurveda College are making their contribution to achieving the goal of a healthy and Viksit Bharat by 2047.
The President w
as happy to note a distinctive feature of the Ayurvedic tradition in Keralam which combines Ayurvedic professional practices with philanthropy. She advised students they should demonstrate how the traditional knowledge-based enterprise and service to the less privileged can be dovetailed, when they enter the professional phase of their life.

title: Vice-President inaugurates New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital in New Delhi
subtitle:
Vice-President calls for collaborative national efforts to strengthen cancer care and research

Benefits of medical research must reach all humanity, not remain confined to a few: Vice-President

Healthcare institutions must combine medical excellence with compassion and affordability: Vice-President

Healthy India is the foundation of Viksit Bharat@2047: Vice-President
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 2:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, today inaugurated the New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital at Okhla, New Delhi. He also released the Holy Family Hospital Souvenir 2026 and felicitated individuals associated with the construction of the new block.
Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated the New Super Specialty Block of Holy Family Hospital in New Delhi today, marking an important step towards expanding access to specialised healthcare.

Highlighting the need for collaborative efforts in cancer care and research, he emphasised that medical advancements must benefit all sections of society.
— Vice-President of India (@VPIndia)
November 27, 2026
Recalling the hospital’s historical legacy, the Vice-President noted that its foundation stone was laid in 1953 by the then Vice-President of India, Dr. Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan. He said that the continuity of this legacy reflects how institutions founded with noble intentions continue to serve society across generations.
Appreciating the hospital’s commitment to providing healthcare irrespective of caste, creed, religion or economic status, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that the philosophy of India’s civilisational ethos rests on mutual respect and the freedom of every individual to practise their faith. He observed that good initiatives and selfless service must always be encouraged and celebrated.
Highlighting the importance of collaborative efforts in combating cancer, the Vice-President called for creating a common forum bringing together cancer treatment institutions across the country to share research, knowledge and best practices. He emphasised that the benefits of medical research and innovation must reach all sections of humanity and should not remain confined to a few countries or privileged sections. He expressed his willingness to take initiatives towards strengthening such collaboration.
The Vice-President said that the new Super Specialty Block would expand access to specialised healthcare. He observed that the success of such facilities would ultimately depend on their ability to combine advanced medical treatment with affordability, compassion and a human touch.
Referring to the Government’s efforts under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the Vice-President highlighted the expansion of India’s healthcare infrastructure. He noted that initiatives such as Ayushman Bharat and PM Jan Arogya Yojana have helped reduce the financial burden of hospitalisation on economically weaker families. He also highlighted the significant increase in AIIMS institutions, medical colleges and MBBS and postgraduate medical seats over the past decade, bringing specialised healthcare and medical education closer to people across the country.
Emphasising that the vision of Viksit Bharat@2047 must ensure that the benefits of development reach every citizen, including those in villages and smaller towns, he said that charitable hospitals and voluntary organisations are important partners in strengthening India’s healthcare ecosystem.
Stressing that infrastructure and advanced equipment alone cannot define a hospital’s strength, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan said that its real strength lies in the dedication, expertise and human touch of its healthcare professionals. He observed that a healthy society is indispensable for building a developed nation and called for collective efforts towards sustainable and inclusive development.
Reverend Andrea Francia, Chargé d’Affaires, Apostolic Nunciature in India; Reverend Archbishop Anil J. T. A., Director, Holy Family Hospital, and other dignitaries were present on the occasion

title: LOK SABHA SPEAKER PAYS TRIBUTES TO SHRI G. V. MAVALANKAR ON HIS BIRTH ANNIVERSARY
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 1:45PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Lok Sabha Speaker Shri Om Birla paid floral tributes to Shri Ganesh Vasudev Mavalankar, the first Speaker of Lok Sabha, in the Central Hall of Samvidhan Sadan, today, on his birth anniversary.
Deputy Chairman, Rajya Sabha, Shri Harivansh; Members of Parliament; former Members; Secretary-General, Lok Sabha, Shri Utpal Kumar Singh and other dignitaries also offered floral tributes.
Shri Mavalankar, born on 27 November 1888 in Baroda (present-day Gujarat), played a monumental role in shaping India’s parliamentary institutions. Beginning his legislative journey in 1937 as a member of the Bombay Legislative Assembly from Ahmedabad, he served as its Speaker until 1946. He later presided over the Sixth Central Legislative Assembly, guiding it through the crucial years leading to Independence.
After 1947, Shri Mavalankar served as Speaker of the Constituent Assembly (Legislative) and subsequently as Speaker of the Provisional Parliament. With the formation of the First Lok Sabha in 1952, he was unanimously elected as its Speaker on 15 May 1952, a responsibility he fulfilled with distinction until his demise on 27 February 1956. His vision, discipline and commitment continue to define the functioning and traditions of the Indian Parliament.
The portrait of Shri Mavalankar, painted by Shri Madhav Satawalekar, decorates the Lobby of Samvidhan Sadan. It was unveiled by the then Prime Minister Pt . Jawaharlal Nehru on 7 September, 1956.
संविधान सदन के केंद्रीय कक्ष में आज लोकसभा के प्रथम अध्यक्ष, श्री गणेश वासुदेव मावलंकर जी की जयंती पर पुष्पांजलि अर्पित की।

श्री मावलंकर जी का जीवन स्वतंत्रता संग्राम, सार्वजनिक सेवा और संसदीय लोकतंत्र के प्रति उनकी अटूट निष्ठा का प्रेरक उदाहरण है। स्वतंत्रता आंदोलन में सक्रिय योगदान देने के साथ उन्होंने संविधान सभा और अंतरिम संसद में भी महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका निभाई। लोकसभा के प्रथम अध्यक्ष के रूप में उन्होंने सदन की कार्यवाही के संचालन, संसदीय नियमों और प्रक्रियाओं की मर्यादा तथा अध्यक्ष पद की निष्पक्षता के ऐसे मानदंड स्थापित किए, जिन्होंने भारतीय संसदीय परंपराओं को सुदृढ़ आधार प्रदान किया।

वे केवल एक कुशल संसदीय संचालक ही नहीं, बल्कि प्रखर राष्ट्रसेवी, समाजसेवी और शिक्षाविद् भी थे। सदन में सभी दलों और सदस्यों के अधिकारों के प्रति उनकी सजगता, धैर्यपूर्ण कार्यशैली और लोकतांत्रिक मूल्यों के प्रति प्रतिबद्धता उनके व्यक्तित्व की विशिष्ट पहचान रही। भारतीय संसदीय व्यवस्था की आधारभूत परंपराओं को आकार देने में उनका योगदान सदैव स्मरणीय रहेगा। उनका जीवन सार्वजनिक जीवन में शुचिता, कर्तव्यनिष्ठा और संस्थागत गरिमा बनाए रखने की प्रेरणा देता रहेगा।

title: India’s Growth Story Remains Strong, Resilient and Trustworthy Amid Global Uncertainties: Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal
subtitle:
Shri Goyal Calls for Greater Long-Term Investments and a Broader Credit Ecosystem

Shri Goyal Stresses Need for Innovative Financing Instruments to Support India’s Growth Ambitions

Shri Goyal Highlights 12 Years of Economic Reforms, Resilience and Expanding Market Opportunities

Shri Goyal Emphasises Export Growth, Manufacturing Investments and Value Addition to Make India a Global Manufacturing Hub
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 12:09PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Minister of Commerce and Industry Shri Piyush Goyal today said that India’s growth story remained strong, resilient and trustworthy despite global uncertainties, with the country delivering on the trust placed in it by the world. Addressing the India Debt Capital Market Summit 2026, he highlighted India’s economic performance, sustained reforms, expanding trade opportunities and the growing importance of debt markets in supporting the country’s development ambitions.
The Minister said India had delivered 7.8 per cent growth in the first quarter of the current financial year and expressed confidence that the country was on track to maintain its growth momentum in the second quarter as well. Gross fixed capital formation had increased by about 12 per cent, while exports had already reached USD 570 billion in the first seven months of the year. He said India was well on track to achieve its USD 1 trillion export target, which had appeared unimaginable and aspirational when it was set in May this year. Credit growth of about 19 per cent was another positive indicator, particularly for credit markets.
Shri Goyal said India had demonstrated resilience amid two ongoing wars, an oil price shock, uncertainties surrounding tariffs and global trading opportunities, disruptions to sea routes and sporadic attacks affecting air travel. Despite these challenges, the world's trust in India's growth story had remained constant, and the country had delivered on that trust.
He said India had continued to reform processes, introduce policies, improve ease of doing business and maintain an open-door policy to engage with businesses and stakeholders. The Government was planning for the next 20 to 25 years, with the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047 firmly embedded in the system and the ambition of becoming a USD 30 trillion economy. The objective was to ensure that every child born in the country had access to a better quality of life, good education, healthcare and greater opportunities.
The Minister said India had continued to finalise free trade agreements (FTAs) and reform the GST system to make it simpler and reduce tax rates, thereby boosting consumption. He noted that GST collections continued to rise, with October recording an all-time high. Exports also registered a record performance in October, reaching USD 90 billion in a single month.
He said several substantive FTAs had not yet come into effect. The India-EU FTA was expected to be signed later this year and come into effect by March or April next year. The India-US trade deal was also close to culmination, with the process and pathway for finalising the agreement beginning to take shape, he added.
Congratulating the organisers for bringing together the entire debt capital market ecosystem on a common platform, the Minister said the summit's theme, ‘Catalysts, Apex and Credit’, was contemporary and critical to India's growth story. He said the bond and credit markets embodied the importance of trust, as they depended on the trustworthiness of borrowers.
Shri Goyal said India's trusted partnership with countries around the world was central to its engagement in preferential, bilateral and free trade agreements. The country's growth story was anchored in the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, the opportunities offered by a USD 4 trillion economy progressing towards USD 30 trillion, and the trusted partnerships India offered to its global partners.
The Minister said India had now emerged as a preferred partner, an attractive investment destination and a trusted companion for the next two to three decades. He highlighted the country's expanding manufacturing and export capabilities, its integration with the global economy through FTAs, and the rapid development of infrastructure.
He said India was expected to construct more buildings in the next 30 years than the entire existing stock of residential and commercial buildings in the country. This reflected the scale of infrastructure development and the opportunities emerging across sectors.
Shri Goyal said that while rising oil prices had a significant impact on an economy, their implications for India's long-term growth needed to be assessed in the context of the country's changing economic fundamentals. He noted that India had significantly higher foreign exchange reserves, remittances and foreign direct investment inflows than it had 20 years ago.
He said India was exporting over USD 700 billion, while its overall export basket was expected to reach USD 1 trillion this year. The country had a GDP of USD 4 trillion, placing it among the world's top five or six economies. On a purchasing power parity basis, India's GDP was approximately USD 18 to 19 trillion, demonstrating its capacity to absorb goods and services and produce at competitive prices.
The Minister said that at India's current economic scale, fluctuations of a few dollars in oil prices could not determine the country's long-term future. He noted that India continued to have among the lowest levels of national debt in the world, with its external debt being significantly lower within its overall debt. These factors demonstrated the sustainability of India's growth story. He emphasised that India had never defaulted on its obligations to the world, including during the COVID-19 pandemic.
Shri Goyal said India continued to have moderate interest rates and expressed confidence in the country's economic prospects. He noted that domestic institutional investors and retail investors had supported the markets through periods of volatility, including when foreign investors were withdrawing funds. He said India's growth story remained safe, strong, resilient and trustworthy.
The Minister emphasised that India's economic transformation was the result of 12 years of sustained reforms and transformational initiatives across sectors, rather than coincidence or luck. He highlighted the Government's focus on meeting the daily needs of citizens, including food, clothing, shelter, healthcare, education, good roads, quality electricity and digital connectivity.
He also highlighted the Jal Jeevan Mission's efforts to provide water to every household in every village and said that bringing 50 crore people out of poverty in 12 years was a significant achievement. As incomes rise and people move into the new middle class, middle class and upper middle class, they would create substantial market opportunities.
Shri Goyal said infrastructure development, rising consumption and economic growth, together with FTAs opening up new markets, would create opportunities for India's manufacturers, agricultural exporters, seafood exporters and service providers. He expressed confidence that India would continue to grow while undertaking steady reforms and making sustained efforts to improve the lives of its people.
The Minister called for taking India's exports to the next level and increasing investments in manufacturing to make the Make in India initiative a globally competitive manufacturing base. He emphasised the need for greater value addition and quality in India, along with building a larger pool of talent to enable the country to participate at the forefront of emerging technologies such as artificial intelligence, machine learning and quantum computing.
He said India was a global partner and highlighted the expansion of its preferential market access through FTAs. Until 2014, India's FTAs covered countries with a combined GDP of approximately USD 10 trillion, against a global GDP of about USD 115 trillion. He said the nine FTAs covering 38 developed countries finalised in the last four and a half to five years covered a GDP of USD 60 trillion. Together with the earlier agreements, India now had preferential market access to economies accounting for USD 70 trillion of global GDP.
The Minister said India was negotiating eight or nine additional agreements and expected to add another USD 15 trillion in market access, taking the total to USD 85 trillion out of a global GDP of USD 115 to 120 trillion. He said almost every country in the world wanted to enter into an FTA with India, reflecting the country's growing position as a trusted partner and the opportunities available for Indian businesses.
Referring to the summit's theme, Shri Goyal said the Government and the private sector were collectively catalysing new growth opportunities, while opening doors for higher capital expenditure by both. The upward trend in credit growth reflected the attractiveness of India's growth story and the renewed opportunities for investment.
He said the expansion of semiconductor fabrication facilities, electricity grids, data centres and the next port coming up in Vadhavan outside Mumbai would collectively generate substantial debt requirements in the economy. The Minister said debt markets would play an important role in financing India's growth and called for the country's financing system to match the scale, diversity and duration of the opportunities emerging over the next two to three decades. He emphasised the need for faster and more efficient financing, along with attractive and innovative instruments to meet the economy's debt requirements.
He said private capital would become an increasingly meaningful source of capital in the coming years. India's inclusion in global bond indices would also play an important role in the growth of debt markets.
The Minister outlined five key priorities for the debt capital market ecosystem:
First, he called upon bond issuers, including large corporates, public sector undertakings and infrastructure developers, to make the bond market their first port of call for capital expenditure, including for longer-gestation projects. He emphasised the need to develop innovative solutions to meet their financing requirements.
Second, he urged investors to support long-term debt and the broader credit ecosystem. He said insurance companies, pension companies, pension funds, provident funds and mutual funds were increasingly holding patient capital and encouraged them to look beyond AAA-rated instruments.
Third, he called upon the market to make bonds easier to trade and enable transactions to take place instantaneously, on the lines of the share market.
Fourth, he urged exporters and their financiers to translate the opportunities created by FTAs into investment decisions and build capacity to serve the markets that had opened up.
Fifth, he reiterated that the Government was open to working with all stakeholders and invited suggestions and ideas from the sector on further reforms and improvements.
The Minister concluded by expressing confidence in India's continued growth and resilience, and emphasised the importance of collaboration between the Government and the private sector in realising the country's economic ambitions.

title: India to Host ITU Plenipotentiary Conference 2030; Union Minister Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia Invites Global Telecommunications Community to India
subtitle:
Union Minister extends warm invitation to Member States, global experts and industry leaders to join India in 2030

PP-26 has formally accepted India’s proposal to host PP-30 followed by approval by ITU council-2026

India's hosting of PP-30 marks a significant milestone in the country's growing engagement with global telecommunications and digital governance
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 10:30PM by PIB Delhi
content:
In a moment of great pride for India and a significant milestone in its engagement with the international telecommunications community, India will host the International Telecommunication Union's (ITU) highest policy making body Plenipotentiary Conference in 2030 (PP-30). India’s proposal to host PP-30 has now received formal acceptance at the Plenipotentiary Conference 2026 (PP-26) concluded on 27 November 2026 at Doha, Qatar, following its earlier approval by the ITU Council at its 2026 session in Geneva.
Union Minister for Communications and Development of North Eastern Region, Shri Jyotiraditya M. Scindia, extended a warm invitation to the global telecommunications community through a video message in presence of ITU leadership and PP-26 delegates, inviting representatives of Member States, global telecommunications experts, policymakers, industry leaders and delegates to join India for the landmark Conference in 2030.
In his video message, Shri Scindia expressed India's sincere gratitude to all Member States for the confidence reposed in the country, both through its election to the ITU Council for the 2027–2030 term and the opportunity to host the next Plenipotentiary Conference.
Describing these mandates as both an honour and a responsibility, the Union Minister reaffirmed India's commitment to working alongside all Member States towards building a connected, inclusive and digitally empowered world.
Emphasising India's deep rooted cultural ethos of
'Atithi Devo Bhava'
, Shri Scindia said that India looks forward to welcoming the global telecommunications community not only to experience its rich civilisational heritage and vibrant cultural diversity, but also to witness its remarkable journey of technological transformation, innovation and digital inclusion.
He assured Member States that India is fully committed to organising a successful, inclusive and memorable Conference, providing an enriching platform for dialogue, collaboration and international cooperation.
Calling upon Member States to view PP-30 as an opportunity to deepen international partnerships and advance shared global priorities, Shri Scindia said, "Let us come together in India in 2030—not merely to convene a Conference, but to strengthen our bonds of friendship, deepen international cooperation and shape a more connected, inclusive and digitally empowered future for all
."
The formal acceptance of India's invitation at PP-26 follows a sustained engagement with the ITU. The Government of India first submitted its formal expression of interest to host PP-30 in November 2024, followed by formal proposals to the ITU Council 2025 and subsequently in 2026 session, the Council approved India's invitation and agreed to transmit it to PP-26 for formal acceptance. The acceptance by the Plenipotentiary Conference now marks the completion of this process and affirms the international community's confidence in India's capacity to host this important global gathering.
At the outset of his video message, Shri Scindia conveyed his appreciation to the Government and people of Qatar for their gracious hospitality and excellent arrangements for PP-26. He also congratulated the incoming leadership of the ITU and wished them success in advancing the Union's objectives.
India's Growing Engagement with the ITU
India has been an active member of the International Telecommunication Union since 1869 and a continuous member of its Council since 1952. Over the years, India has contributed to the Union's work across telecommunications standardisation, radio communication and digital development.
The country's successful hosting of the World Telecommunication Standardization Assembly (WTSA-24) in New Delhi in October 2024 further demonstrated India's ability to convene the global telecommunications community and contribute to discussions on emerging technologies, 6G, Artificial Intelligence, Digital Public Infrastructure and sustainable digital transformation.
The Plenipotentiary Conference is the highest policy-making body of the ITU and is convened every four years. It brings together representatives of Member States to determine the Union's overall direction, adopt its strategic and financial plans, and elect its senior leadership and Council.
India's hosting of PP-30 will provide an important opportunity to strengthen multilateral engagement, deepen cooperation among Member States and contribute to shaping the future of global telecommunications and digital technologies.
India looks forward to welcoming the global telecommunications community in 2030.

title: TRAI releases “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 4:52PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today released
“The Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026”
. The amendment regulations modernise the framework governing Reference Interconnect Offer (RIO), align it with the current licensing and authorisation regime, and update the framework for determination of Significant Market Power (SMP), submission and publication of RIO, the Model RIO and RIO Guidelines, and interconnection arrangements. A financial disincentives framework for specified contraventions has also been introduced by these regulations. These regulations will come into force with effect from 1st January 2027.
Interconnection in telecommunications refers to the commercial and technical arrangements through which authorised entities or licensees connect their telecommunication equipment, networks and services so that users can access the users, services and networks of other authorised entities or licensees. Sub-clauses (ii), (iii) and (iv) of Section 11(1)(b) of the TRAI Act, 1997,
inter alia
, require TRAI to prescribe the terms and conditions of interconnection between service providers, ensure technical compatibility and effective interconnection between service providers, and regulate arrangements among service providers for sharing revenue derived from the provision of telecommunication services.
The Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) Regulation, 2002 was notified in July 2002 to ensure transparent, non-discriminatory and standardised interconnection terms, particularly where a service provider has Significant Market Power (SMP). Since then, the telecom sector has undergone significant technological and regulatory changes, including the transition from legacy circuit-switched and E1/TDM-based interconnection towards packet-switched, IP-based networks and the emergence of LSA-level interconnection.
To ensure that the existing regulatory framework governing interconnection matters remain relevant, transparent, and conducive to efficient interconnection between service providers, TRAI initiated a review of the regulatory framework through a Pre-Consultation Paper on the “Review of existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, dated 03.04.2025.
Subsequently, a Consultation Paper on the “Review of existing TRAI Regulations on Interconnection matters”, providing the background information and taking into account the stakeholders’ comments received during the pre-consultation process, was issued on 10.11.2025. Through the Consultation Paper, stakeholders’ comments were sought,
inter alia
, to review the Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) Regulation, 2002.  After extension, the last dates for furnishing written comments and counter-comments were 15.12.2025 and 29.12.2025, respectively.
In response to the issues raised in the Consultation Paper, seventeen stakeholders submitted their comments, while nine stakeholders submitted counter-comments. As part of the consultation process, an Open House Discussion (OHD) on the Consultation Paper was held on 28.01.2026. Based on the comments received from stakeholders during the consultation process, and its own analysis, TRAI has finalised the Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026.
The salient points of the amendment regulations are given below:
Periodic determination of Significant Market Power (SMP)
: A service provider will be regarded as having SMP if it holds a share of 30% or more in any one or more of the “Activity” parameters in a licensed or authorised telecommunication service area. The four parameters are Adjusted Gross Revenue, Subscriber Base, Voice Call Handling Capacity of the Network and Volume of Traffic. SMP will be determined by TRAI in respect of each of the four services, namely, Wireline Access Service, Wireless Access Service, National Long Distance Service and International Long Distance Service, in each licensed or authorised telecommunication service area based on the data furnished by service providers. After the end of the first quarter of every financial year, the determination will be based on Subscriber Base as on 31st March, and the maximum Voice Call Handling Capacity of the Network and Volume of Traffic for the month of March, of the preceding financial year. A subsequent determination may be made taking into account Adjusted Gross Revenue for the preceding financial year, without affecting the SMP status already determined for that financial year. The amendment regulations also provide that a service provider once determined by TRAI to have SMP shall continue to be treated as having SMP until TRAI modifies its SMP status.
Time-bound submission and publication of RIO
:
A service provider determined to have SMP must submit its RIO to TRAI for approval within 30 days of such determination, and publish the approved RIO on its website within 15 days of its approval. Where TRAI directs modification of a published RIO, the modified RIO must be submitted to TRAI within 15 days of such direction, and any modified RIO, after approval, must be published within 15 days of its approval. This will ensure timely public availability of approved interconnection terms and conditions, and help new entrant service providers plan network interconnection and commence negotiations without avoidable delay.
Transparency and flexibility in interconnection agreements
: Interconnection agreements are to be entered into in accordance with the published RIO. Service providers may, by mutual consent, modify the terms and conditions of the published RIO while entering into an interconnection agreement. The published RIO provides an accessible and non-discriminatory baseline, while mutually agreed modifications preserve commercial flexibility and can reduce negotiation time and inter-operator disagreements.
Updated interconnection routing framework:
The revised framework provides simplified routing arrangements for PSTN-PSTN, PSTN-PLMN, PLMN-PLMN, PSTN-NLD Network and PLMN-NLD Network, incoming and outgoing traffic routing for intra-LSA, inter-LSA and international calls, based on LSA-level interconnection. By replacing obsolete SDCA/LDCA-based routing with LSA based routing, the framework will simplify network planning, support scalable IP-based architecture and facilitate more efficient delivery of traffic across service providers.
Modernised model RIO and RIO guidelines
:
The legacy model RIO and guidelines have been updated. The revised framework reflects LSA-level points of interconnection, IP-based interconnection, current technical standards, and updated quality requirements. This provides an updated and consistent reference for entering into interconnection agreements.
Graded framework for financial disincentives
: For contravention of provisions relating to submission, modification, publication of RIO, and furnishing of data by service providers for determination of SMP, a graded financial disincentive subject to a ceiling per Service Area for each instance of contravention has been prescribed. The framework provides a reasonable opportunity to represent before imposition of financial disincentive. The graded structure distinguishes short delays from prolonged non-compliance, encourages timely corrective action, and strengthens enforcement while retaining proportionality and procedural fairness.
Collectively, the amendment regulations are expected to strengthen transparency, regulatory certainty and non-discrimination in interconnection arrangements, while supporting efficient interconnection in an IP-based and LSA-level network environment.
The full text of “The Telecommunication Interconnection (Reference Interconnect Offer) (Amendment) Regulations, 2026”, along with the Explanatory Memorandum, is available on TRAI’s website
www.trai.gov.in
.

title: TRAI extends use of the 1601-series for Service and Transactional Voice Calls to Additional Sectors under Phase-II
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 4:51PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has today issued a Direction extending the use of the 1601-series, allocated by the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) to the eligible entities in the sectors other than BFSI sector and Government, exclusively for making service and transactional voice calls to their customers.
Under the second phase of implementation of 1601-series, entities in the following sectors will be eligible for the allocation of numbers from this series subject to the specified eligibility criteria:
a) Retail Chains, e-Commerce, Hospitals, Diagnostic Laboratories, Telecom Service Providers, Internet Service Providers (ISPs), Automobile Sales, Automobile Repair and Servicing, Travel Agencies, Commercial Airlines, Food Aggregators, Ride-hailing Aggregators and Lending Service Providers (LSPs). Only the entities having an annual turnover of Rs. 500 crore or more in at least one of the preceding three financial years shall be eligible.
b) Distribution Platform Operators (DPOs) such as Direct-to-Home (DTH), Headend-in-the-Sky (HITS), Internet Protocol Television (IPTV) service providers and Multi-System Operators (MSOs), having a subscriber base of one million or more in any month during the preceding twelve months.
c)  The 1601-series numbers shall be assigned only to the companies registered in India under the applicable law.
Earlier, under the first phase of implementation, TRAI vide its Direction dated 10th August, 2026, allowed allocation of 1601-series numbers to the utilities, and logistics and courier services sectors.
A trusted numbering series for consumers
The 1601-series is a designated series exclusively for service and transactional voice calls by the entities in sectors other than BFSI and Government, and its use for making promotional voice calls is strictly prohibited. Being a trusted channel, the numbers from this series are allocated only to the verified entities, and thereby helping consumers to easily identify legitimate service and transactional calls. This measure is an important tool in combating impersonation by fraudsters who use normal 10-digit numbers and falsely claim to represent legitimate businesses.
Time-bound onboarding and reporting
Access Providers have been directed to complete onboarding and migration of all eligible entities within 180 days from the date of issuance of the Direction. They shall publicise the availability of the series among eligible entities, submit status reports to TRAI every fifteen days, and submit a final compliance report within fifteen days after the expiry of 180-day implementation period. Based on a review of the implementation, the Authority may notify additional sectors or eligible entities from time to time.

title: INSTITUTE OF AEROSPACE MEDICINE HOSTS 65TH ANNUAL CONFERENCE OF THE INDIAN SOCIETY OF AEROSPACE MEDICINE (ISAM)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 10:50PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The 65th Annual Conference of the Indian Society of Aerospace Medicine (ISAM) was held at the Institute of Aerospace Medicine (IAM), Bengaluru on               26 - 27 November 2026. The conference was inaugurated by Air Chief Marshal Ashutosh Dixit, Chief of the Air Staff (CAS), in the presence of military and civil dignitaries from the country and abroad. Themed 'One Airspace - One Mission: Aeromedical Support from Runway to Orbit', the conference portrayed a unified vision of Aerospace Medicine that seamlessly spans military aviation, civil aviation and human spaceflight and the pivotal role of aeromedical support in ensuring safety, performance and mission success from runway operations to orbital missions.
The event served as a melting pot of expertise, bringing together Defence Forces personnel, IAF aircrew and scientific stalwarts from ISRO, DRDO and HAL. Air Marshal Vivek Hande, DGMS (Air), delivered Presidential Address, stressing the pivotal role of aerospace medicine in maximizing aircrew efficiency and ensuring the viability of human life in orbit.
The conference upheld its tradition of intellectual excellence with the Air Marshal Subroto Mukerjee Memorial Oration, delivered by Shri APVS Prasad, CE CEMILAC. This prestigious platform, which has previously seen the likes of Dr APJ Abdul Kalam and Wing Commander Rakesh Sharma, remains a cornerstone of the society's academic heritage.
The Air Vice Marshal MM Srinagesh Memorial Oration, dedicated to the 'Father of Aviation Medicine', was delivered by Air Vice Marshal Anupam Agarwal (Retd). The ‘JHF Manekshaw Panel’ featured expert insights from Wing Commander Surender Sodhi (Retd), Chief Advisor of Aeromedical Services, MD ONBOARD (Canada) and Colonel KN Rao (Retd), Technical Officer, ICAO (Canada). Aligning with the conference's spaceward focus, the Cosmonaut Rakesh Sharma Lecture Series, moderated by Cosmonaut Wg Cdr Rakesh Sharma, featured a keynote address by     Mr Pawan Chandana, Co-founder and CEO of Skyroot Aerospace.
The scientific agenda was both rigorous and diverse, exploring everything from altered gravity and spaceflight medicine to the psychological rigours of civil aviation.
Key discussions revolved around crew performance optimization, indigenous aircraft design and the critical safety window from ejection to environmental extremes. High-impact panels also tackled the evolution of women in fighter flying and the bridging of terrestrial simulations with orbital flight, while young investigators presented pioneering research that signalled the future of the field.

title: DELIVERY OF VINDHYAGIRI DESIG (Y3024) (PROJECT 17A INDIGENOUS ADVANCED STEALTH FRIGATE)
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 6:04PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vindhyagiri
(Yard 3024), the
seventh and final
ship of Nilgiri class (Project 17A) and the third of the class built by Garden Reach Shipbuilders and Engineers Ltd (GRSE), was delivered to the Indian Navy on
27 Nov 26
at GRSE, Kolkata, marking the successful
culmination of Project 17A ship deliveries
and a major milestone in achieving self-reliance in warship design and construction.
Project 17A frigates are versatile multi-mission platforms, designed to address current and future challenges in the maritime domain. Named after the Vindhyagiri mountain range in Karnataka, the ship is a reincarnation of the erstwhile INS Vindhyagiri, a Leander-class frigate, that was part of the Indian Navy fleet from 08 Jul 1981 to 11 Jun 2012, rendering 31 years of glorious service to the nation. This state-of-the-art frigate reflects a quantum leap in naval design, stealth, firepower, automation and survivability and is an admirable symbol of
Aatmanirbharta
in warship building.
Designed by the Warship Design Bureau (WDB) and overseen by the Warship Overseeing Team (Kolkata), P17A frigates reflect a generational leap in indigenous ship design, stealth, survivability and combat capability. These ships feature an advanced suite of weapons and sensors compared to the P17 (Shivalik) class. The ships are configured with Combined Diesel or Gas (CODOG) propulsion plants, comprising a diesel engine and a gas turbine that drive a Controllable Pitch Propeller (CPP) on each shaft, and a state-of-the-art Integrated Platform Management System (IPMS). The potent and technologically advanced weapons and sensors suite significantly enhances the ships’ multi-dimensional warfare capabilities across anti-surface, anti-air and anti-submarine domains.
Delivery of
Vindhyagiri
marks a historic milestone wherein all seven P17A frigates have been delivered to the Indian Navy within a span of
23 months
from the delivery of the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri) on 20 Dec 24 (
https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=2086668
). Furthermore, the institutional experience gained from the construction of preceding six P17A ships enabled a significant compression of the build period of
Vindhyagiri
to
68 months
, in comparison to 84 months taken for the first-of-class (INS Nilgiri). Delivery of
Vindhyagiri
showcases the design, ship construction and engineering prowess of the nation and reflects Indian Navy’s unrelenting focus of
Aatmanirbharta
in both ship design and ship building. With an
indigenisation content of 75%,
the project has involved
over 200 MSMEs
and has enabled
employment generation of approx. 4000 personnel directly and more than 10000 personnel indirectly
.

title: Vice-President Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan to inaugurate the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0
subtitle: KTS 5.0 to be held from November 28 to December 12, 2026 in Varanasi
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 1:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Vice-President of India, Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, will inaugurate the fifth edition of Kashi Tamil Sangamam (KTS) to be held from 28 November to 12 December 2026, in Varanasi. Union Minister for Defence, Shri Rajnath Singh, is scheduled to attend the valedictory session. The Event will bring together over 1,400 delegates to celebrate the centuries-old cultural, linguistic and civilisational ties between Tamil Nadu and Kashi.
The initiative, inspired by the vision of Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi, seeks to strengthen the bonds between the two regions and promote the spirit of
Ek Bharat Shreshtha Bharat
. The fifth edition will celebrate the timeless wisdom and ethical teachings of the
Thirukkural
, one of the most celebrated works of Tamil literature.
The Event is organized by the Department of Higher Education, Union Ministry of Education, in collaboration with IIT Madras, Banaras Hindu University (BHU), Central Institute of Classical Tamil (CICT), Uttar Pradesh Government and several Central Govt Departments and Ministries.
Theme for KTS 5.0 - “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”
The theme of Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 is “Thirukkural Payilvom – Thirukkural Abhyas Karen”, meaning “Let us Learn the Thirukkural”. The focus is on fostering awareness and understanding of the timeless wisdom of the
Thirukkural
, particularly among students and youth, while encouraging appreciation of India's rich literary traditions and enduring cultural heritage.
The
Thirukkural
, authored by the celebrated Tamil poet and philosopher Thiruvalluvar, is one of the most enduring works of Tamil literature and continues to offer guidance across generations. Its 1,330 couplets explore ethics, governance, human relationships, compassion, discipline and responsible living. The text is divided into three parts, Aram (Virtue), Porul (Wealth) and Inbam (Love), encompassing the principles of righteous conduct, social and political life, and human relationships.
Delegates and Itinerary
Around 1,400 participants from Tamil Nadu, organised into seven groups of around 200 persons each, will undertake an eight-day journey. It comprises four days of travel and four days of visits and structured programmes. The itinerary covers Varanasi, Prayagraj and Ayodhya, with cultural, academic, domain-specific and spiritual engagements.
The participants come from seven categories:
• Students
• Teachers
• Writers and Media Professionals
• Agriculture and Allied Sectors
• Professionals and Artisans
• Women
• Spiritual leaders
During their stay in Varanasi, delegates will visit prominent religious, historical and cultural sites, including Kashi Vishwanath Temple, Ramnagar Fort and Bharat Mata Temple. The itinerary also includes Ganga Aarti, Ganga Snan, academic sessions and cultural programmes. Delegates will subsequently visit the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj and Shri Ram Temple in Ayodhya.
A special Tamil heritage circuit will take delegates to Mahakavi Subramania Bharati’s ancestral house, Kedar Ghat and Kashi Matham in Little Tamil Nadu, along with an academic interaction at BHU’s Tamil Department.
Students' Engagement Programme
A nationwide Students' Engagement Programme is being undertaken through 1,000 Higher Education Institutions to promote wider understanding of the
Thirukkural
among students from diverse academic disciplines and linguistic backgrounds. It will include structured study, research, and campus-based activities.
•Each participating institution will assess its interested students on the
Thirukkural
and nominate one student on merit.
•The selected students will attend an online academic orientation, offered in 22 scheduled languages and English.
•A one-month research and academic engagement will follow, with multilingual study material from CICT. Each eligible selected student will be entitled to a stipend of ₹10,000, subject to the programme guidelines and completion of the prescribed requirements.
•Each student will write an article or research note of 4 to 10 pages under a faculty guide and give a one-hour presentation on the
Thirukkural
at their institution.
Thirukkural Teaching in Schools of Uttar Pradesh
During the Sangamam, 50 teachers from Tamil Nadu will visit Uttar Pradesh and teach the
Thirukkural
in schools.
Thirukkural
experts from Tamil Nadu will also visit schools in Varanasi. They will introduce students to the core values of the text through orientation modules, interactive sessions and quizzes.
Reading Sessions in Schools
The National Book Trust, in association with the Rashtriya e-Pustakalaya, will conduct interactive sessions in schools in Varanasi on reading habits, storytelling and creative activities.
Academic Engagements, Cultural Showcases and Regional Craft Exhibitions
Banaras Hindu University will co-host a National Conference on the
Thirukkural
, with the Bharatiya Bhasha Samiti as a partner. Cultural programmes and screenings of short films on the
Thirukkural
will also be organized. Handicraft and handloom outlets from Tamil Nadu and Uttar Pradesh will be set up for the delegates at the main venue.
Digital and Public Outreach
Kashi Tamil Sangamam 5.0 will also use technology to make the teachings of the
Thirukkural
accessible to a wider audience across India. The
Thirukkural
multilingual app of CICT carries all 1,330 couplets with translations into 22 scheduled languages. CICT's programme for the Edition also includes short animated videos and films on selected couplets, and
Thirukkural
audiobooks.

New Centre to Strengthen Technology Infrastructure and Support IT/ITeS Enterprises, Startups and Technology-led Entrepreneurship in the Rohilkhand Region

Initiative Aims to Promote Innovation, Facilitate Business Opportunities and Encourage Employment Generation in the Region

content:
Software Technology Parks of India (STPI), a premier S&T organisation under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), Government of India,
inaugurated its
Bareilly Centre
in Uttar Pradesh. The centre was inaugurated by
Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India
, in the presence of
Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh; Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly and Smt.
Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI among other dignitaries.
The inauguration marks an important milestone for STPI as Bareilly becomes its
75th centre
in the country, further expanding its nationwide network and commitment to strengthening India's technology ecosystem beyond established metropolitan hubs. Of STPI's 75 centres,
67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities
, reflecting its sustained focus on decentralising technology infrastructure and enabling regional entrepreneurship. Developed with an investment of approximately
₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel,
the Bareilly Centre will strengthen the regional IT/ITeS ecosystem by providing an institutional platform for technology enterprises and emerging entrepreneurs.
Shri Jitin Prasada, Minister of State for Electronics and Information Technology, and Commerce & Industry, Government of India, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly centre is a landmark gift not only for Bareilly, but for the youth of the entire Rohilkhand region
especially Pilibhit, Shahjahanpur, and Badaun so they no longer have to migrate to major hubs like Mumbai, Noida, and Hyderabad for IT, startups, incubation, innovation, and research, instead gaining world-class technical facilities right at home while shaping the future of coming generations and driving local job creation. "In the IT sector, India stands today as the world's Talent Capital, powered by youth technical skill and design capabilities, and providing free technical facilities through STPI alongside skill development and support ensures that financial constraints never hold back talent and enterprise. As local MSMEs, IT industries, chambers of commerce, and entrepreneurs utilize the center to full capacity, we will expand additional buildings and technical facilities, while Common Service Centers (CSCs) under Digital India continue expanding rural access to Aadhaar, banking, electricity bill payments, and citizen services—giving me complete confidence, alongside commendations to STPI Director General Arvind Kumar and his team, that like Noida, Kanpur, Lucknow, and Gorakhpur, Bareilly will emerge as a major IT hub propelling technical and economic growth across Rohilkhand.”
Dr. Arun Kumar Saxena, Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Forest & Environment, Zoological Garden and Climate Change, Government of Uttar Pradesh, said, “The establishment of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a welcome development for the region and will contribute to expanding opportunities in the technology sector. Bareilly and the surrounding areas have considerable potential in terms of talent and entrepreneurship. The centre will provide an important platform for young people, startups and technology enterprises to explore new opportunities, develop innovative ideas and contribute to the state's economic progress.”
Shri Chhatrapal Singh Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Bareilly, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is a significant milestone for the region. It will help create a stronger foundation for technology-led entrepreneurship and provide aspiring entrepreneurs and young professionals with access to a wider ecosystem of opportunities.
Smt. Shruti Gangwar, Member of Parliament, Rajya Sabha, said, “The inauguration of the STPI Bareilly Centre is an encouraging development for the region, particularly for its young talent and aspiring entrepreneurs. Access to technology infrastructure and a supportive startup ecosystem can help unlock local potential, encourage innovative thinking and create new avenues for professional growth. ”
Shri Arvind Kumar, Director General, STPI, said, “The inauguration of the Bareilly Centre marks a significant milestone in STPI's journey, taking our nationwide network to 75 centres, of which 67 are located in Tier-II and Tier-III cities. This reflects our continued commitment to extending technology infrastructure and entrepreneurial opportunities beyond established IT hubs and enabling emerging regions to participate in India's digital economy. Developed with an investment of approximately ₹18.25 crore on a 2-acre land parcel, the Bareilly Centre is an important addition to this network and will provide an enabling environment for IT/ITeS enterprises, startups and aspiring entrepreneurs in the Rohilkhand region. Through our infrastructure, incubation initiatives and industry linkages, we aim to nurture local talent, facilitate business growth and support the development of innovative technology-led enterprises.”
The Bareilly Centre further expands STPI's nationwide presence and its efforts to promote the IT/ITeS industry beyond established technology hubs. Through its network of centres, incubation facilities and entrepreneurship initiatives, STPI continues to support startups and technology enterprises through infrastructure, industry linkages and opportunities for product development and intellectual property creation.
The event was also attended by several prominent dignitaries and public representatives
.
The inauguration marks an important step towards strengthening Uttar Pradesh's regional technology ecosystem, encouraging entrepreneurship and enabling technology-led economic growth through greater collaboration among government, industry, academia and startups.

Software Technology Parks of India (STPI) is a premier S&T organization under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), engaged in promoting the IT/ITES industry, innovation, research and development, startups, and product and intellectual property creation in emerging technology domains. These include the Internet of Things, blockchain, artificial intelligence, machine learning, computer vision, robotics, augmented and virtual reality, animation and visual effects, and data science and analytics. STPI supports innovation across domains such as gaming, fintech, agritech, medtech, autonomous and connected mobility, ESDM, cybersecurity, Industry 4.0 and drones.

title: NBA disburses Rs. 13.76 Crore  in ABS Funds across 28 States and 4 UTs: Linking Commercial Utilisation of Medicinal Plants with Biodiversity Conservation

content:
The National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) has disbursed Rs. 13.76 crore to promote biodiversity conservation and sustainable use of biological resources across 28 States and 4 Union Territories. The allocation forms part of the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) contributions received from AYUSH products manufacturing companies for the commercial utilisation of medicinal plants and other plant-based biological resources.
These contributions pertain to three applications involving the utilisation of a total of 234 plant species. These biological resources were procured through market and trader networks, making it difficult to identify the individual benefit claimers associated with their supply chains. However, considering the majority of the medicinal plants used by companies are from forest areas, the State forest cover and occurrence of medicinal plants in the State/UT are taken into account for disbursing the benefit-sharing amount.
Among the 234 plant species, ten species, namely Guggul, Ashwagandha, Bhringraj, Punarnava, Sarpagandha, Kalmegh, Black Pepper, Indian Gooseberry, Gokhura and Shalparni, contributes for a benefit-sharing amount of Rs.
6.45 Crore, out of Rs. 13.76 Crore. The ABS mechanism provides a means to channel the monetary benefits arising from their commercial utilisation towards biodiversity conservation, sustainable harvesting and promoting cultivation of these valuable biological resources. The funds transferred can support strengthening of local biodiversity governance, Biodiversity Management Committees (BMCs), updating People’s Biodiversity Registers, documentation of biological resources and associated traditional knowledge, research and capacity building, community-led conservation, restoration of degraded ecosystems, sustainable harvesting and cultivation practices, and biodiversity-based livelihood initiatives. The NBA has so far collected Rs. 278 crore
through the ABS mechanism, of which around Rs. 218.86 crore has been disbursed towards biodiversity conservation and benefit-sharing initiatives across the country.
India’s ABS framework contributes to the global biodiversity agenda and the implementation of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). The Yerevan Pathway, adopted at CBD COP 17 (19–30 October 2026), emphasises resource mobilisation, scientific and technical cooperation, and accelerated implementation of biodiversity targets. India’s ABS mechanism supports these priorities by advancing Target 13 of the KMGBF on fair and equitable benefit sharing from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge.
Medicinal plants are an integral part of India’s biological wealth, traditional healthcare systems and rural livelihoods. They support communities engaged in their collection, cultivation, processing and trade, while the associated traditional knowledge forms an important part of India’s cultural heritage. The growing commercial utilisation of medicinal plants underscores the need for responsible sourcing, sustainable harvesting and conservation of wild populations. The ABS mechanism facilitates benefit sharing from their utilisation, supporting biodiversity conservation, strengthening local institutions and promoting community-based livelihoods. These efforts complement Government initiatives such as the National AYUSH Mission, National Medicinal Plants Board programmes and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana, which promote medicinal plant cultivation, value addition and livelihood generation.

content:
In recognition of its sustained outreach efforts, engaging public-facing formats and citizen-centric communication, the GST & Customs Pavilion of the Central Board of Indirect Taxes and Customs (CBIC) has been awarded the Bronze Medal for Display at the 45th India International Trade Fair (IITF) 2026 at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi, today.
CBIC showcased its flagship ‘GST & Customs Pavilion’ at IITF 2026 from 14th–27th November 2026. The Pavilion was inaugurated on 16th November 2026 by Shri Vivek Chaturvedi, Chairman, CBIC, in the presence of Members of the Board and senior officers.

More than 1 lakh people visit the CBIC Pavillion across age groups, professions and sectors, reflecting strong public interest in CBIC’s reform and facilitation initiatives.
Key highlights of the CBIC Pavilion
1. Expert helpdesks for on-the-spot assistance
8 dedicated helpdesks covering GST, Customs, GSTN, Invoice Registration Portal (IRP), ICEGATE and CPGRAMS, manned by officers and domain experts, assisted visitors with GST registration, return filing, refunds, e-invoicing, customs procedures, baggage provisions, import-export facilitation and grievance redressal.
2. Awareness on Next-Gen GST Process Reforms and Baggage Rules, 2026
Special emphasis was placed on explaining the Next-Gen GST Process Reforms and the updated Baggage Rules, 2026, helping taxpayers and international travellers understand the simplified procedures and their entitlements.

Digital displays and educational material showcased CBIC’s technology-driven transformation, highlighting greater transparency, efficiency and ease of compliance. [Educational videos and tutorials were available in X regional languages besides Hindi and English.]

Virtual Reality (VR) games, mechanical games like catch the baton and gold bar, ventriloquist and puppet shows, coloring competition for kids and interactive quizzes, magic shows, Augmented Reality (AR) selfie zones, regional dances, Nukkad Nataks (street plays) made tax and customs awareness fun and accessible for visitors of all ages, especially children and youth.

title: Dr Abhilaksh Likhi, Union Secretary Visits College of Fishery Science, Nagpur; Interacts with Fisheries students, Highlights Emerging Opportunities in Fisheries, Aquaculture, entrepreneurship and the Blue Economy
subtitle: Emphasises Cluster-Based Development and Technological Interventions in the Fisheries Sector
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 4:14PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Dr. Abhilaksh Likhi, Secretary, Department of Fisheries, Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry and Dairying, Government of India, visited the College of Fishery Science, Nagpur, Maharashtra.
He delivered a presentation on ‘India’s Initiatives in the Fisheries and Aquaculture Sector​,’ highlighting key developments and emerging opportunities in the sector​,​ and interacted with students on the growth, emerging opportunities and future prospects of India's fisheries sector. The College promotes experiential learning through hands-on training, complemented by smart classroom teaching in areas such as fish breeding, hatchery & farm management, value added processing.
Highlighting the sector's major achievements, Dr. Likhi stated that India's total fish production has reached to
198 lakh tonnes
in 2024-25. India stands as the world’s second largest aquaculture producer accounting for 8% of the global fish production. Inland fisheries and aquaculture production have registered substantial growth and achieved
153 lakh tonnes
in 2024-25. India's seafood exports have also reached an all-time high of
₹73,890.46 crore (USD 8.45 billion)
in FY 2025-26, with export volumes touching 19.32 lakh metric tonnes. Seafood exports have registered a significant growth at an all-time high. The sector supports the livelihoods of over
3 crore
fishers and fish farmers.
In his presentation, the Union Secretary emphasised the Government's commitment to strengthening the fisheries value chain, and highlighted the importance of the cluster-based development approach in facilitating economies of scale, improving productivity and creating integrated opportunities across production, processing, marketing and exports. He informed that the Government of India has notified
34 specialised fisheries
and aquaculture clusters across the country, focusing on end-to-end value chain solutions and catering to diverse species including tuna, shrimp, pearl spot, murrel, pangasius, tilapia, trout, seaweed, ornamental fisheries, reservoir fisheries, coldwater fisheries, cage culture, organic fisheries and riverine fisheries, among others. These clusters are envisaged as integrated development hubs, addressing gaps across pre-production, production and post-harvest activities while facilitating technology adoption, market linkages and value addition. The cluster approach will also leverage institutional financing and support from agencies such as NABARD, along with participation from private entrepreneurs and other stakeholders.
He also focused on
technology infusion
in transforming fisheries and aquaculture into a modern, productive and commercially sustainable fisheries sector. He elaborated on the adoption of advanced aquaculture technologies such as Recirculatory Aquaculture Systems (RAS), Biofloc, reservoir and sea cage culture, raceways, pen culture and improved hatchery and seed production systems, supported under the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY). He also emphasised the growing role of digital technologies, Artificial Intelligence (AI), Internet of Things (IoT), machine learning and drone-based applications in improving water quality monitoring, fish health management, feeding practices, disease surveillance and operational efficiency.
Highlighting the Government's efforts to promote entrepreneurship and strengthen the institutional ecosystem, he spoke about the opportunities being created for
fisheries start-ups
, young entrepreneurs, Fisheries Farmer Producer Organisations (FFPOs), cooperatives and Self-Help Groups (SHGs) through various initiatives, including PMMSY and the Pradhan Mantri Matsya Kisan Samridhi Sah-Yojana (PM-MKSSY). He emphasised the importance of strengthening fisheries cooperatives and FFPOs, improving their access to institutional credit, financial assistance, and capacity-building and digital market platforms such as the Open Network for Digital Commerce (ONDC). He also highlighted the role of the National Fisheries Digital Platform (NFDP) in formalising the sector and facilitating access to credit, insurance and other scheme benefits.
He further underscored the need for modern fisheries infrastructure to strengthen the entire value chain, including Smart and Integrated
Fishing Harbours
,
modern fish landing centres,
wholesale and retail fish markets, cold-chain facilities, transportation and logistics networks, processing units and value-added product development. He highlighted emerging opportunities in diversified fisheries segments such as seaweed cultivation, ornamental fisheries, pearl culture and other mariculture activities, which can create additional livelihood and entrepreneurial opportunities, particularly for youth and women. He also stressed the importance of improving post-harvest management, processing and value addition to enhance income realisation for fishers and fish farmers and strengthen India's position in global seafood markets.
Fisheries students from various fisheries colleges and universities across the country, representatives from Krishi Vigyan Kendras (KVKs), ICAR institutes and the Departments of Fisheries of various States and Union Territories, attended through video conferencing. The Secretary encouraged students to look beyond conventional employment avenues and explore emerging opportunities across various segments of the fisheries and aquaculture sector. During the interaction, College of Fishery Science students shared their views and perspectives on the sector and highlighted the need for an information-sharing platform to facilitate access to internship and employment opportunities. They also showed keen interest in learning about various schemes and initiatives of the Government of India that could support self-employment and entrepreneurship in the fisheries sector.
Dr. Likhi also visited various facilities of the College of Fishery Science, Nagpur, Maharashtra, including fish seed unit, hatcheries, exhibition, and museum. He also visited the Fisheries Technology Complex, envisioned as a comprehensive, one-stop facility for inland fisheries, integrating research, training, diagnostics and demonstration services. The complex is being e​stablished under the​Fisheries and Aquaculture Infrastructure Development Fund (FIDF) scheme of the Government of India, with a project cost of Rs 19.69 crore.

title: Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava Inaugurates Advanced Spectral CT Facility at NIMHANS, Bengaluru; Reviews Key Mental Healthcare and Brain Health Initiatives
subtitle:
Smt. Srivastava Reviews NIMHANS’ Suicide Prevention Programmes and Capacity-Building Initiatives to Strengthen the Mental Health Workforce Across Four Professional Disciplines

Tele-MANAS Crosses 50 Lakh Calls; Expansion of Helpline Integration, Counsellor Training, Quality Assurance and Technology-Enabled Mental Health Services Reviewed

NIMHANS Centre for Addiction Medicine Treats 25,913 Individuals Between January and October 2026; Strengthens Telemedicine Follow-ups, Specialised Treatment and Nationwide Outreach

NIMHANS suicide prevention initiatives reach 37 government hospitals across Karnataka; 31,557 survivors receive interventions under Urban Self-Harm Study

Karnataka Brain Health Initiative (KaBHI), Developed by NIMHANS and State Government with NITI Aayog's Consultation, Conducts 2.61 Lakh Screenings and Treats 32,630 Patients; MoHFW task Force Proposes National- Level Replication
ministry: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 8:01PM by PIB Delhi
content:
Union Health Secretary Smt. Punya Salila Srivastava inaugurated and dedicated an advanced Spectral CT facility at the Emergency Block of the National Institute of Mental Health and Neuro Sciences (NIMHANS), Bengaluru, today. During her visit, the Secretary reviewed the Institute's major initiatives and its contributions to national efforts in mental healthcare, suicide prevention, addiction treatment, capacity building and brain health.
The newly commissioned facility is equipped with the Revolution Apex Elite CT scanner from GE, a 256-detector-row system featuring advanced spectral imaging and AI-based image reconstruction. Designed to support comprehensive neurological, cardiac, vascular and whole-body imaging for both adults and children, the scanner will operate round the clock to cater to the substantial patient load at the Emergency Department.
The advanced imaging system is expected to strengthen emergency diagnostics, particularly in stroke and neurovascular care, where timely and accurate diagnosis is critical. It enables rapid identification of brain haemorrhage, arterial blockages and other life-threatening conditions, while also supporting the evaluation of cardiac and vascular disorders, post-interventional complications, polytrauma and other complex medical conditions.
Review of National Mental Healthcare Initiatives
During the visit, the Secretary reviewed the progress of Tele-MANAS (Tele Mental Health Assistance and Networking Across States), which has crossed the milestone of 50 lakh calls. The programme has steadily expanded its reach through integration with other helplines, nationwide awareness initiatives, counsellor training and accreditation, quality assurance measures and technology-enabled services. Its five-year vision for 2027–32 focuses on expanding access, enhancing service quality and integrating Tele-MANAS more closely with the broader healthcare system.
The Secretary also reviewed the activities of the Centre for Addiction Medicine (CAM), NIMHANS, one of the six centres supported under the Ministry's Tobacco Control and Drug De-addiction Programme. Between January and October 2026, the Centre provided treatment to 25,913 individuals with addictive disorders, with more than 7,000 receiving telemedicine follow-ups.
Its specialised services include opioid substitution treatment, neuromodulation, counselling and tele-aftercare. The Centre also reaches healthcare professionals across the country through digital training and e-learning programmes. Its Addiction Rx mobile application has recorded approximately 19,600 downloads across 145 countries. Community outreach activities include initiatives under the Nasha Mukt Bharat Abhiyaan and the Tobacco Quitline, which has received over 36,000 calls. The Centre is working towards expanding its training programmes and digital consultation services, alongside developing AI-enabled tools to facilitate early identification of addiction, particularly among young people.
Strengthening Professional Capacities and Suicide Prevention
The review also covered the NIMHANS–CIP–LGBRIMH Capacity Building Programme, undertaken in collaboration with the Central Institute of Psychiatry (CIP), Ranchi, and Lokopriya Gopinath Bordoloi Regional Institute of Mental Health (LGBRIMH), Tezpur. The programme aims to strengthen professional capacities in Psychiatry, Clinical Psychology, Psychiatric Social Work and Psychiatric Nursing.
Another key area of review was the work of the NIMHANS Suicide Prevention, Research, Implementation, Training and Engagement (N-SPRITE) Centre, aligned with the four pillars of the National Suicide Prevention Strategy (2022).
The Centre's Urban Self-Harm Study (USHAS) has recorded 42,382 cases since 2022, with 31,557 survivors receiving interventions and a reported re-attempt rate of 1.3%. The Centre is now operational in 37 government hospitals across Karnataka. It also implements SURAKSHA, YASHAS and EMPOWER, focusing on community, youth and workplace suicide prevention.
Smt. Srivastava was also apprised of the recently launched Wellness Centre, NIMHANS Student Mental Health Services. The Centre provides dedicated counselling, psychotherapy and psychiatric support to students through a multidisciplinary team. Its services include structured short-term therapy, referrals for long-term care wherever needed and psychiatric consultations twice a week.
Advancing Brain Health and Emergency Neurological Care
The discussions also covered NIMHANS' efforts to strengthen brain health and neurological care across Karnataka. The Karnataka Brain Health Initiative (KaBHI), of NIMHANS and the State government, developed with NITI Aayog’s consultation, focuses on the early detection, prevention and treatment of neurological disorders. The initiative has conducted 2.61 lakh screenings and provided treatment to 32,630 patients.
The National Task Force on Brain Health, constituted by the Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, has proposed KaBHI as a model for national-level initiatives. Complementing these efforts, the proposed Hub and Spoke Model for Head Trauma and Stroke Care in Karnataka aims to improve access to timely emergency neurological care through regional hubs and coordinated referral networks. The proposed model includes a Neurohub at KMCRI, Hubballi, and an Acute Stroke Emergency and Assessment Centre at NIMHANS.
The Government of India remains committed to strengthening comprehensive and accessible healthcare, with mental health forming an integral part of this effort. Through initiatives spanning early diagnosis, treatment, suicide prevention, addiction care, professional capacity building and brain health, the Ministry continues to support efforts towards improving access to quality healthcare services and strengthening the mental healthcare ecosystem across the country.

title: At 57th IFFI, a Story of How the Entire Crew of ‘The River Train’ Stepped into a Child’s World
subtitle:
The Argentine Feature Brings Together Childhood Dreams and the Spirit of Collaboration

‘The River Train’ captures the universal desire to explore the unknown and find one’s own path in life
content:
Goa, 27 November 2026
The cast and crew of the Spanish language film
The River Train (El Tren Fluvial)
, - producer Valentine Torre and actor Rita Pauls - spoke about how trust, friendship and sensitivity shaped the making of the film at a press conference organized today on the sidelines of the 57th International Film Festival of India (IFFI) in Goa. Directed by Lorenzo Ferro and Lucas A. Vignale, the 75-minute Spanish-language feature from Argentina had its India premiere in the International Competition section of IFFI 2026.
Set in the Argentine Pampas, the film follows nine year old Milo, who trains in Malambo, a traditional Argentine folk dance, but dreams of travelling by train to Buenos Aires, a city he knows only through films. As he ventures out on his own, unfamiliar encounters and moments of loneliness lead him to discover a world beyond the expectations placed upon him. His journey explores childhood, freedom and the challenges of pursuing one’s dreams.
Recalling the origins of the project, Mr. Torre said it began as an informal invitation among friends to make a small film. What started as a modest undertaking gradually grew into a feature through mutual trust and collective effort, eventually reaching international audiences at film festivals in Berlin, San Sebastián and Buenos Aires.
Ms. Pauls, who plays the Professor in the film, spoke about working with Milo Barría, a young Malambo dancer with no previous acting experience. Rather than expecting the child to adapt to the demands of a conventional film set, the crew adjusted its working methods to his needs and moods, she said. She explained that this flexibility allowed the young actor to remain at the centre of the creative process.
Speaking about the film’s visual style, the producer explained that the 4:3 aspect ratio was inspired from the directors’ admiration for classic cinema while also helping the team work within its production budget. The use of black-and-white imagery in parts of the film evokes the atmosphere of older cinema and lends a dreamlike quality to the narrative.
Looking ahead, Mr.Torre shared that the team plans to begin shooting
Plan de fuga
, a road film about two brothers, in 2027. He also spoke about the recent theatrical release of
The River Train
in Spain and expressed hope for future filmmaking collaborations in India.
Through Milo’s journey,
The River Train
captures the universal desire to explore the unknown and find one’s own path in life. Its making also offers a reminder that meaningful cinema can emerge from modest beginnings when creative ambition is matched by empathy and collective effort.
The session was moderated by Anushka Sarkar.
