title: CSIR-CRRI Wins Prestigious CII 4R Awards 2026 for Pioneering Steel Slag Road Technology and ECOFIX; recognized among India's Top 30 Waste-to-Worth Leaders
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 4:58PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The CSIR-Central Road Research Institute (CSIR-CRRI), New Delhi, has been conferred the prestigious CII 4R Awards 2026 under the category of “Excellence in Innovative Solutions for Sustainable Waste Management by Research Labs/Academic Institutions.” The Institute has also been recognized among India's Top 30 Waste-to-Worth Leaders for its pioneering Steel Slag Road® Technology and ECOFIX® – Iron and Steel Slag-based Instant Pothole Repair Mix, which transform industrial waste generated by the steel industry into valuable materials for sustainable road construction and maintenance.
The awards were presented on 26th November 2026 during the 11th International Conference on Waste-to-Worth Technologies at Hotel the Lalit, New Delhi. Dr. Ch. Ravi Sekhar, Director, CSIR-CRRI, and Shri Satish Pandey, Scientist G and Head, Flexible Pavement Division, CSIR-CRRI, received the award on behalf of the Institute from Prof. Anil Gupta, prominent Indian scholar of grassroots innovation and founder of the Honey Bee Network.
Speaking on the occasion, Shri Satish Pandey, Scientist G and Head, Flexible Pavement Division, CSIR-CRRI, and inventor of the Steel Slag Road® and ECOFIX® technologies, highlighted the enormous potential of these innovations in addressing the challenge of industrial waste generated by India's steel industries. He emphasized that the steel industry generates approximately 30 million tonnes of steel slag and that CSIR-CRRI's technologies enable the scientific processing and use of steel slag as processed aggregates for sustainable road infrastructure. These innovations offer an effective pathway for converting large-scale industrial waste into valuable construction materials, reducing dependence on conventional natural aggregates and promoting circular economy practices in the road sector.
Transforming Industrial Waste into Sustainable Infrastructure
The Steel Slag Road® Technology, developed by CSIR-CRRI, demonstrates the utilization of scientifically processed steel slag aggregates in road construction. It provides a sustainable pathway for converting steel industry by-products into valuable road construction materials, promoting resource efficiency and reducing the environmental burden associated with industrial waste disposal and extraction of natural aggregates.
Similarly, ECOFIX®, an iron and steel slag-based instant pothole repair mix, offers an innovative solution for road maintenance through the productive utilization of industrial by-products. Its commercialization by RAMUKA GLOBAL SERVICES under a CSIR-CRRI technology license demonstrates how indigenous research can be translated into market-ready solutions through effective collaboration between research institutions and startups.
Together, these technologies exemplify the principles of a circular economy by transforming industrial waste into valuable resources for infrastructure development. title: New technology developed for stable, tunable and scalable white LEDs
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 3:27PM by PIB Delhi
content:
An innovative way to avoid colour blurring using Halide Perovskite Nanocrystals can enable stable, scalable, flexible, and cost-effective white-lighting technologies suitable for white light emitting diodes and smartphones.
The commercial white light-emitting diodes (WLEDs) used in our homes and smartphones are extremely energy-efficient, but they have a few drawbacks. They rely on expensive, rare-earth elements and complex, high-temperature manufacturing. Furthermore, once built, the tone of the white light is fixed and cannot be adjusted.
To find a simpler, tunable, and more cost-effective alternative, researchers are looking toward a new class of materials called all-inorganic halide perovskite nanocrystals (chemical formula CsPbX₃, where X can be chlorine, bromine, or iodine) which are bright, low cost and emit exceptionally bright and pure colors.
However, these Perovskite nanocrystals suffer from a critical drawback known as anion exchange. When nanocrystals of different halide compositions—such as green-emitting CsPbBr₃ and red-emitting CsPbI₃—come into close contact, their halide ions rapidly migrate and swap between crystals. As a result, the two intended colors blend into an unwanted intermediate orange color and with this color blurring can occur within minutes.
A team of researchers from the Centre for Nano and Soft Matter Sciences (CeNS), Bengaluru — an Autonomous Institute under the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India — in collaboration with the Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Delhi, has developed an innovative dual-protection strategy to lock the colors in place.
Fig.
Demonstration of perovskite-based phosphor-converted WLEDs, their individual components, and a real-time photograph of the operational pc-WLED. The WLEDs were fabricated on both glass and flexible PET substrates. Green and red micropatterning was achieved through spray coating to fabricate the micropatterned WLED.
First, the team consisting of Gauri Sharma, Swati Khurana, Sameer Sapra, Pralay K. Santra reduced the halide vacancies on the crystal surface with a material called lead selenide. This removed the primary pathway for ion migration without degrading the material's brightness or color.
Second, they introduced atomic layer deposition (ALD) encapsulation by depositing an ultrathin, transparent protective coating of aluminum oxide (alumina, Al₂O₃) — only about 5 to 6 nanometers thick. This layer acts as a physical barrier that blocks ions from diffusing between adjacent color-emitting layers.
Using a simple and scalable spray-coating technique together with micropatterning, the researchers fabricated multi-layered white-LED devices on both rigid glass and flexible plastic (PET) substrates. The devices operated continuously for up to 24 hours in optimised versions — with stable white emission whose colour stayed close to that of ideal white light even when heated and cooled. They also established that tone of the white light can be converted to dim or warm tone just by changing the electrical current.
This work published in the journal Small represents an important step toward stable, scalable, flexible, and cost-effective white-lighting technologies but needs a bit of refinement to handle the toxicity of lead and find ways of making it eco-friendly before hitting the general market.

subtitle: Joint initiative to empower adolescent girls and young women through skills, confidence-building and livelihood opportunities across 100 districts in 24 States/UTs
ministry: Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 9:15PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) will jointly launch the second phase of NAVYA –
Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls
(NAVYA 2.0) on 28 November 2026 at 3:30 PM at the Uttarakhand Sanskrit Academy Auditorium, Haridwar.
Building on the learnings of its pilot phase, NAVYA 2.0 aims to advance women-led development by nurturing the aspirations of adolescent girls and young women, strengthening their capabilities and enabling them to achieve greater confidence, self-reliance and economic independence.
The programme will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon’ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development; Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Smt. Rekha Arya, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Madan Kaushik, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; and Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand.
The launch programme will feature the formal launch of NAVYA 2.0 by the Hon’ble Union Ministers. It will also include the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand, and distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).
NAVYA: Nurturing aspirations and enabling empowerment
NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of MWCD and MSDE that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women. The initiative recognises that empowerment goes beyond training and entails nurturing aspirations, building confidence, developing capabilities and enabling informed choices about the future.
The pilot phase was launched on 24 June 2025 in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, with an envisaged coverage of 27 Aspirational Districts across 19 States. Approximately
1,200 adolescent girls
were trained in industry-relevant job roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Solar PV Installation Helper and Fashion Designer. The initiative also emphasised digital and financial literacy, career readiness and entrepreneurship to strengthen their confidence and socio-economic independence.
NAVYA 2.0: Expanding the horizons of empowerment
Building on the pilot experience, NAVYA 2.0 will expand its reach to
100 districts across 24 States/UTs
, with a particular focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. The eligible age group has also been widened from 16–18 years to 16–25 years, bringing a larger cohort of adolescent girls and young women within its ambit.
The expanded initiative will provide greater access to vocational training in industry-relevant, new-age and non-traditional job roles, while strengthening pathways to employment,
apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. It
places emphasis on institutional convergence, coordinated district-level implementation and outcome-oriented support. A structured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to facilitate effective coordination and implementation at the district level.
Technology-enabled implementation
The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) will serve as the digital platform for facilitating access to skilling opportunities and supporting candidates throughout their journey from enrolment to training and certification. It will also enable real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress and certification, strengthening transparency and accountability. Digitally verifiable credentials will further help candidates demonstrate their skills and competencies.
Advancing women-led development
Through the convergence of MWCD and MSDE, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, pursue their aspirations and participate meaningfully in economic and social development.
NAVYA 2.0 is a step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment, enabling every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme Provides Financial Assistance of up to ₹ 3.50 Lakh to SC and ST Patients for Treatment of Life-Threatening Diseases
subtitle:
SC and ST Patients with Annual Family Income of up to ₹5 Lakh Eligible for Medical Assistance under the Revised Scheme

Scheme Covers Heart Surgery, Kidney Surgery, Dialysis, Cancer Treatment, Brain Surgery, Organ Transplantation, Spinal Surgery and Other Life-Threatening Diseases

Eligible Beneficiaries To Log In https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 7:21PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF), an autonomous body under the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment, Government of India, is implementing the revised
‘Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme’
, providing financial assistance of up to
₹
3.50 lakh
to eligible patients belonging to the Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) suffering from serious and life-threatening diseases.
Director DAF Shri Vinesh Pachnanda said the revised scheme, notified on June 2, 2026, aims to improve access to specialised healthcare services and reduce the financial burden of medical treatment on economically vulnerable families. It seeks to ensure that financial constraints do not become a barrier to accessing essential medical treatment and surgical interventions, he said.
Shri Pachnanda said under the revised provisions, individuals belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes whose
annual family income does not exceed ₹
5 lakh
are eligible to apply for financial assistance.
The scheme covers serious ailments related to the kidney, heart, liver, brain and cancer, besides organ transplantation, spinal surgery and other life-threatening diseases requiring medical or surgical intervention, he added.
Under the scheme,
100% of the estimated cost of surgery or covered treatment, subject to the prescribed financial ceiling
, is released directly to the concerned hospital, Shri Pachnanda added.
The Director said the maximum financial assistance admissible is ₹1.50 lakh for heart surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney surgery or dialysis, ₹2.50 lakh for cancer surgery, chemotherapy or radiotherapy, ₹2 lakh for brain surgery, ₹3.50 lakh for kidney or organ transplantation, ₹1.50 lakh for spinal surgery and ₹2 lakh for other life-threatening diseases.
The financial assistance may be released in a single instalment before surgery directly to the concerned hospital through RTGS, NEFT or Demand Draft, thereby reducing the immediate financial burden on patients and their families, the Director added.
Recognising the financial challenges associated with prolonged medical treatment, the revised scheme also enables patients suffering from chronic ailments to seek a second renewal grant in the subsequent financial year, subject to the applicable provisions, he said.
Shri Pachnanda further said a significant provision of the revised scheme is the inclusion of beneficiaries covered under the
Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (PM-JAY)
who are suffering from renal diseases or require kidney or organ transplantation.
Such beneficiaries are also eligible to seek medical assistance under the Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme while other patients covered under PM-JAY are not eligible for assistance under the scheme, he clarified.
To facilitate access to specialised medical treatment across the country, the scheme is implemented through a wide network of recognised healthcare institutions, including the All India Institute of Medical Sciences (AIIMS), New Delhi, and AIIMS in other States, all Central Government Health Scheme (CGHS)-approved hospitals, hospitals attached to State Government medical colleges, State Government hospitals, hospitals recognised by State Governments and hospitals fully funded by the Central or State Governments, Shri Pachnanda informed.
The scheme also covers Government hospitals located at district headquarters and major towns where facilities for the treatment of serious and life-threatening diseases, including organ transplantation and spinal surgery, are available, he added.
Shri Pachnanda informed several specialised healthcare institutions, including Sanjay Gandhi Post Graduate Institute, Lucknow; Patna Medical College Hospital, Patna; Jabalpur Hospital and Research Centre, Jabalpur; B. Barua Cancer Institute, Guwahati; Birla Heart Foundation, Kolkata; Kalinga Hospital, Bhubaneswar; Tata Cancer Research Institute, Mumbai; Nizam Institute of Medical Sciences, Hyderabad; and the Voluntary Health Services, Chennai, are also covered under the scheme.
In exceptional circumstances, treatment at other hospitals may be considered, subject to the satisfaction of the Chairman of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation regarding the merits of the case, he said.
He clarified that applications seeking reimbursement of expenditure already incurred on surgery or medical treatment are ordinarily not entertained. However, reimbursement may be considered on the merits of the case if the application was received by the Foundation at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, he added.
Shri Pachnanda said to ensure transparency and accountability in the utilisation of financial assistance, the concerned hospital is required to submit a Utilisation Certificate along with the final medical bills at the time of discharge of the patient.
The medical aid released to the hospital must be utilised within one month of its release, and any unutilised or balance amount must be returned to the Foundation at the earliest, but not later than one month after the date of discharge of the patient, he said.
The Director DAF informed that eligible beneficiaries may apply for medical assistance through the prescribed application form available on the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation (DAF)
https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/
or submit an application on plain paper containing the requisite details as specified in the prescribed format.
The application must be accompanied by self-attested copies of the latest income certificate, caste certificate and ration card or Aadhaar card of the patient, along with a self-attested passport-size photograph. Applicants are also required to submit the original Estimated Cost Certificate, duly signed by the Medical Superintendent of the concerned hospital, indicating the estimated cost of treatment and the scheduled date of surgery.
In cases involving kidney transplantation, applicants are required to furnish additional documents relating to the relationship between the donor and the beneficiary, the prescribed Form 14 pertaining to the decision of the Authorisation Committee and relevant particulars of the kidney donor. The bank account details of the concerned hospital, including the account number, name of the account holder and IFSC code, may also be provided to facilitate the timely processing and direct transfer of financial assistance.
The duly completed application, along with the requisite documents, must reach
the Director, Dr. Ambedkar Foundation, 15, Janpath, New Delhi – 110001, at least 15 days before the scheduled date of surgery, dialysis or chemotherapy.
The Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme serves as an important intervention in addressing the financial barriers faced by economically vulnerable families belonging to the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in accessing specialised healthcare services. By extending financial assistance for critical medical interventions, the scheme seeks to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure and facilitate timely access to essential healthcare.
Eligible beneficiaries and their family members are encouraged to avail themselves of the benefits under the scheme. Healthcare institutions, State Government departments, social welfare organisations and other stakeholders are also encouraged to disseminate information about the scheme to ensure wider awareness among eligible beneficiaries.
For detailed guidelines, eligibility criteria, recognised hospitals and prescribed application forms, interested applicants may visit the official website of the Dr. Ambedkar Foundation.
https://www.dosje.gov.in/schemes-and-services/dr-ambedkar-medical-aid-scheme/
The implementation of the revised Dr. Ambedkar Medical Aid Scheme reinforces the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment’s commitment to promoting social justice, equitable access to healthcare, financial security and the dignity and well-being of disadvantaged communities, towards the realisation of an inclusive
Viksit Bharat@2047
.

The Ministry of Women and Child Development (MWCD) and the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship (MSDE) will jointly launch the second phase of NAVYA –
Nurturing Aspirations through Vocational Training for Young Women and Adolescent Girls
(NAVYA 2.0) on 28 November 2026 at 3:30 PM at the Uttarakhand Sanskrit Academy Auditorium, Haridwar.
Building on the learnings of its pilot phase, NAVYA 2.0 aims to advance women-led development by nurturing the aspirations of adolescent girls and young women, strengthening their capabilities and enabling them to achieve greater confidence, self-reliance and economic independence.
The programme will be graced by Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon’ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development; Shri Jayant Chaudhary, Hon’ble Minister of State (Independent Charge) for Skill Development and Entrepreneurship and Minister of State for Education, Government of India; Smt. Rekha Arya, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister for Women Empowerment and Child Development, Food and Civil Supplies, Sports and Youth Welfare, Government of Uttarakhand; Shri Madan Kaushik, Hon’ble Cabinet Minister of Panchayati Raj, Disaster Management and Rehabilitation, Ayush and Ayush Education, Reorganization and Census, Government of Uttarakhand; and Shri Trivendra Singh Rawat, Hon’ble Member of Parliament, Lok Sabha, Uttarakhand.
The launch programme will feature the formal launch of NAVYA 2.0 by the Hon’ble Union Ministers. It will also include the inauguration of Saksham Anganwadi Centres and new Anganwadi Centres constructed under PM JANMAN in Uttarakhand, and distribution of certificates to candidates trained under the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY).
NAVYA: Nurturing aspirations and enabling empowerment
NAVYA is a collaborative initiative of MWCD and MSDE that brings together the strengths of the women and child development and skill development ecosystems to empower adolescent girls and young women. The initiative recognises that empowerment goes beyond training and entails nurturing aspirations, building confidence, developing capabilities and enabling informed choices about the future.
The pilot phase was launched on 24 June 2025 in Sonbhadra, Uttar Pradesh, with an envisaged coverage of 27 Aspirational Districts across 19 States. Approximately
1,200 adolescent girls
were trained in industry-relevant job roles such as Drone Manufacturing and Assembly Technician, Solar PV Installation Helper and Fashion Designer. The initiative also emphasised digital and financial literacy, career readiness and entrepreneurship to strengthen their confidence and socio-economic independence.
NAVYA 2.0: Expanding the horizons of empowerment
Building on the pilot experience, NAVYA 2.0 will expand its reach to
100 districts across 24 States/UTs
, with a particular focus on aspirational and hard-to-reach areas. The eligible age group has also been widened from 16–18 years to 16–25 years, bringing a larger cohort of adolescent girls and young women within its ambit.
The expanded initiative will provide greater access to vocational training in industry-relevant, new-age and non-traditional job roles, while strengthening pathways to employment,
apprenticeships and entrepreneurship. It
places emphasis on institutional convergence, coordinated district-level implementation and outcome-oriented support. A structured Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) has also been introduced to facilitate effective coordination and implementation at the district level.
Technology-enabled implementation
The Skill India Digital Hub (SIDH) will serve as the digital platform for facilitating access to skilling opportunities and supporting candidates throughout their journey from enrolment to training and certification. It will also enable real-time tracking of beneficiary registration, attendance, training progress and certification, strengthening transparency and accountability. Digitally verifiable credentials will further help candidates demonstrate their skills and competencies.
Advancing women-led development
Through the convergence of MWCD and MSDE, NAVYA 2.0 seeks to create an enabling ecosystem where adolescent girls and young women, particularly from aspirational and underserved regions, can realise their potential, pursue their aspirations and participate meaningfully in economic and social development.
NAVYA 2.0 is a step towards transforming aspirations into opportunities and opportunities into empowerment, enabling every young woman to shape her own future and contribute to the vision of Viksit Bharat.

title: Ministry of Women and Child Development marks two years of 'Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' Campaign
subtitle:
National level event reinforces collective resolve towards a Child Marriage Free India

States/UTs and stakeholders join the programme at Vigyan Bhawan and through webcast
ministry: Ministry of Women and Child Development
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 7:23PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The Ministry of Women and Child Development today marked two years of the 'Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat' Abhiyaan through a national-level programme at Vigyan Bhawan, New Delhi, in the august presence of the Hon'ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi, Hon'ble Chief Minister of Delhi, Smt. Rekha Gupta, and Hon'ble Minister of State for Women and Child Development, Smt. Savitri Thakur.
The programme brought together representatives of States/UTs, Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs), Child Welfare Committees (CWCs), Ministries and Departments, legal services institutions, international organisations and civil society organisations. It was also webcast to enable officials, frontline functionaries and stakeholders across the country to join the national event. During the programme, participants also took a collective pledge, reaffirming their resolve to work towards making India free from child marriage.
Speaking on the occasion, the Hon'ble Union Minister for Women and Child Development, Smt. Annpurna Devi,​ “Our goal is to ensure that every child in the country gets a safe childhood, every daughter gets the opportunity for education, and they become capable of making their own life decisions—and we have pledged that child marriage will not happen in our home, our neighborhood, or anywhere in the country.” She reiterated that ending child marriage requires sustained action through a 'whole-of-government' and 'whole-of-society' approach and emphasised the importance of education, skilling and empowerment of girls in realising the vision of a Viksit Bharat by 2047.
Smt. Savitri Thakur, Hon’ble Minister of State for Women and Child Development, emphasised the importance of grassroots participation and community-led efforts, highlighting the role of Panchayats, frontline functionaries and community leaders in preventing child marriage. “A Child Marriage Free India is not just a target for 2030; it is an essential step toward realizing the vision of a Developed India (Viksit Bharat) by 2047 under the leadership of the Honorable Prime Minister.”
Smt. Rekha Gupta, Hon’ble Chief Minister of Delhi, called for coordinated efforts by the Government and communities to eliminate child marriage, promote girls’ education and safeguard the rights of children. “A daughter will only progress when we give her the blessing that we will not snatch the book from her hand, we will not marry her off early, and we will give her respect and equal opportunities to move forward.”
The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Campaign was launched on 27 November 2024 with the objective of making Child Marriage Free Bharat. The Campaign focuses on awareness generation, community participation, strengthening the role of CMPOs, timely reporting and intervention, and supporting adolescent girls who are school dropouts or at risk of child marriage through education, skilling and empowerment.
Over the past two years, the Campaign has developed into a sustained nationwide effort. The awareness programmes had reached over 12 crore citizens, while more than 42 lakh pledges had been registered across the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal, MyGov and MY Bharat platforms. The Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal had also emerged as a centralised repository of more than 72,000 Child Marriage Prohibition Officers (CMPOs) across States and Union Territories. The observance is also being held during the ongoing 100-Day Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Awareness Module 2.0, from 21 October to 21 December 2026, aimed at intensifying awareness, mobilisation and coordinated action against child marriage across the country.
Around 700 persons participated in the programme at Vigyan Bhawan. Wider participation was facilitated through webcast, enabling stakeholders across States and Union Territories to join the programme and the nationwide pledge against child marriage. Around 47000 people watched the event via webcast.
The Campaign complements implementation of the Prohibition of Child Marriage Act, 2006 by strengthening the capacity of CMPOs and other duty-bearers and encouraging timely reporting and intervention. Citizens can report incidents, take the pledge and access information and resources through the Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat Portal at
https://stopchildmarriage.wcd.gov.in/
.  Child Helpline 1098, Emergency Response Support System 112 and Women Helpline 181 are also available for assistance and timely intervention.
As Bal Vivah Mukt Bharat completes two years, the Ministry called upon citizens, communities, institutions and all stakeholders to make prevention of child marriage a shared national responsibility and ensure that every child is able to pursue education and realise their full potential.

The upcoming edition will celebrate the values at the heart of the Olympic Movement: good governance and integrity, fair competition and inclusion, the health and welfare of athletes, and a lasting legacy of sustainability and safe sport.
It reflects India's commitment to building its sporting future on ethics, athlete voice and equal opportunity for all, including women and para-athletes, and seeks to inspire the youth to embrace sport and fitness as a way of life.
The movement takes inspiration from Prime Minister's call of

The initiative has evolved into a platform for taking forward Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi’s key national calls and social messages, translating them into action through mass public participation.
Through special editions centred on themes such as Fight Against Obesity, Nasha Mukt Bharat, Pollution Ka Solution, Sundays on Cycle seeks to encourage behavioural change and inspire citizens to contribute to the Prime Minister’s vision of a Fit India and a Viksit Bharat.

title: National Overseas Scholarship Scheme for Scheduled Tribe Students
subtitle: Empowering Aspirations Beyond Borders
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 3:43PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme expands access to international higher education for Scheduled Tribe students through
20 scholarships annually
. With
30% of scholarships earmarked for female candidates
, the scheme promotes inclusive access to global learning opportunities. From 2026-27, it supports Master's and PhD (Doctor of Philosophy) study at universities in the top 1,000 of the QS (Quacquarelli Symonds) World University Rankings. The share of women among beneficiaries rose from 20% in 2015-16, when 3 of the 15 selected candidates were women, to 47.8% in 2024-25, when women accounted for 11 of the 23 selections. Reflecting the Government’s continued support, financial disbursements increased from
₹0.39 crore in 2015-16 to
₹8.00 crore in 2025-26
.
Opening Doors to Global Education
Higher education opens avenues for knowledge, opportunity and professional advancement. According to the
All-India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE) 2023-24, 28,83,218 Scheduled Tribe (ST) students
were enrolled in higher education, up from 21,56,109 in 2019-20. For ST students, international education offers access to specialised knowledge, advanced research opportunities and global academic exposure. Studying at reputed institutions abroad broadens academic horizons, strengthens professional capabilities and opens pathways to diverse career opportunities. Such opportunities help ST students pursue their aspirations while contributing to the development of their communities and the nation.
Recognising the importance of expanding access to global education, the
National Overseas Scholarship (NOS) Scheme for ST Students
seeks to support meritorious tribal students in pursuing higher education abroad. It is a
Central Sector Scheme of the Ministry of Tribal Affairs
, operational since
1954-55
. The scheme offers
20 fresh scholarships
annually for Master's and PhD studies at reputed institutions. It is implemented through Indian Embassies/ Missions abroad under the Ministry of External Affairs.
Over the years, the scheme has undergone significant expansion, reflecting a growing emphasis on widening access to international higher education. From 15 annual scholarships covering engineering, technology and science in 2010-11, the scheme now offers 20 scholarships a year across four fields of study. The wider scope gives ST students more routes to higher study abroad.
Broadening Horizons: The NOS Scheme at a Glance
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme opens avenues for ST students to pursue advanced education at reputed institutions worldwide. It supports Master's and PhD studies at
universities and institutions ranked among the top 1,000 in the QS World University Rankings
. It covers four broad fields of study, each with a set number of slots.

Of the 20 scholarships awarded annually,
17 are allocated to Scheduled Tribe candidates
, while
three are reserved for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs)
. This allocation seeks to ensure educational opportunities for students from particularly disadvantaged tribal communities.
The scheme places particular emphasis on promoting women's participation in international higher education, with
30% of scholarships
earmarked for female candidates. Women made up 20% of the scheme’s beneficiaries in 2015-16 (3 of 15 selections) and 47.8% in 2024-25 (11 of 23 selections). Where the earmarked slots remain unfilled, they are opened to eligible male candidates.

Pathways to Opportunity: Eligibility and Selection Criteria
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme provides a structured eligibility framework to facilitate access to international higher education for deserving ST students. These criteria seek to ensure equitable access to educational opportunities.

Students apply directly to foreign universities and seek the scholarship to fund their studies there. First priority will be given to the candidates who have offer of admission from the top 1,000 ranked foreign Institutes/Universities (as per the latest QS world ranking) and yet to join the Institute as on the date of application. The merit list will be drawn based on the ranking of the Institute. In case of a tie between the QS rankings of two or more candidates, merit will be decided on the basis of marks/grades secured by the candidate in the qualifying examination for higher studies for which the scholarship has been applied for.
One child in a family and one time assistance
Only one child from the same family is eligible for the scholarship, subject to self-certification by the applicant. Each candidate can avail of the scholarship only once and cannot receive another award at the same or higher level under the scheme.
Income Criteria
The applicant's annual family income from all sources must not exceed
₹6 lakh
to be eligible for the scholarship.
Selection
From 2026-27, first priority goes to candidates who hold an offer of admission from a foreign university or institute ranked among the top 1,000 in the latest QS World University Rankings and have yet to join. They are ranked by the QS rank of the institution, and where ranks tie, by marks in the qualifying examination. Any slots left are filled through a personal interview by an expert committee constituted by the Ministry, with preference to candidates who have cleared tests such as the GRE (Graduate Record Examinations), GMAT (Graduate Management Admission Test) or TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language). Selected candidates must secure admission and join an eligible institution within two years of the award letter.
National Overseas Scholarship [NOS] Portal
Applications under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme are invited online through the dedicated
National Overseas Scholarship Portal
. The portal provides information on scheme guidelines, application procedures and documentation requirements, facilitating a streamlined application process. Integrated with DigiLocker, it enables applicants to retrieve existing documents digitally and upload additional documents wherever required. Registered students can also submit queries and grievances directly through the portal. An automated notification system facilitates timely communication through SMS and email alerts, while an integrated dashboard supports effective monitoring of the scheme.
Investing in Aspirations: Financial Assistance under NOS
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme provides financial assistance to ST students throughout their studies abroad. The scheme offers an annual maintenance allowance of USD 15,400 (US Dollars) or GBP 9,900 (British Pounds Sterling) for students pursuing courses in the United States and United Kingdom, respectively. For other countries, the applicable allowance is provided in US dollars or at equivalent rates. An annual contingency and equipment allowance of USD 1,532 or GBP 1,116 is provided for expenses such as books, essential apparatus, study tours, typing and thesis binding.
The scholarship also covers tuition fees and other compulsory, non-refundable fees charged by educational institutions, along with actual visa fees and applicable poll taxes. Medical insurance premiums are reimbursed at actual rates, subject to assessment by the respective Indian Embassy or Mission. Incidental journey expenses of up to USD 20 or its equivalent in Indian rupees are permissible.
To facilitate international travel, the scheme provides economy-class airfare from India to the nearest destination serving the educational institution and back. The airfare is reimbursed at actual cost, subject to the shortest route and best available fare. Provision is also made for local travel between the arrival point and the place of study, including second-class rail fares. Where rail connectivity is unavailable, admissible bus, ferry or connecting air travel expenses are covered under the prescribed provisions.
The Government’s financial disbursements under the National Overseas Scholarship Scheme have increased substantially over the years. The amount disbursed rose from
₹0.39 crore in 2015-16 to
₹8.00 crore in 2025-26
, reflecting the Government’s continued efforts to strengthen financial support for ST students pursuing higher education abroad. The number of students supported in a year, new and continuing, rose from 8 in 2013-14 to 64 in 2025-26, and 400 students in all received support over the period. Since 2014-15, the Ministry has released ₹46.46 crore to help eligible Scheduled Tribe students pursue higher education abroad under the scheme.
Expanding Reach
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme has extended international higher education opportunities to Scheduled Tribe students across India. As a Central Sector Scheme with pan-India coverage, it offers 20 fresh scholarships every year, open to eligible ST students from all States and Union Territories, with no State-wise or district-wise allocation of seats or funds. This reflects the Government’s continued efforts to widen access to overseas education for tribal students.
Beyond Borders: Empowering Tribal Aspirations
The National Overseas Scholarship Scheme reflects the Government's commitment to expanding international higher education opportunities for Scheduled Tribe students. By reducing financial barriers, the scheme can enable deserving tribal youth to pursue advanced academic and research opportunities at reputed institutions abroad. Exposure to global learning environments can strengthen specialised knowledge, enhance professional capabilities and open new avenues for career advancement. These opportunities can also promote socio-economic mobility and inspire future generations of tribal students to pursue higher educational aspirations.
Each selection round is announced on the dedicated
National Overseas Scholarship Portal
, where eligible ST students can check application dates and apply. By widening access to global education, the scheme supports inclusive educational development for tribal communities and contributes to the vision of a Viksit Bharat.

title: NHRC, India takes suo motu cognizance of the reported continuous rise in TB cases in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh amidst Tuberculosis Free India campaign
subtitle:
Reportedly, only 1.43 lakh out of 1.77 lakh registered patients in 2024 received a single instalment of financial assistance of Rs. 1,000 per month under a government nutrition scheme

The Commission issues a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks
date:
प्रविष्टि तिथि:
                27 NOV 2026 8:06PM by PIB Delhi
content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report regarding the continuous rise in the number of registered tuberculosis (TB) patients in Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh. Reportedly, registered TB patients in Bhopal have increased by about 19 per cent from 10,773 in 2022 to 12,850 in 2024. According to the media report, these figures have emerged even as there is a Tuberculosis Free India campaign going on in the country. Further, only 1.43 lakh out of 1.77 lakh registered patients in 2024 reportedly received a single instalment financial assistance of Rs. 1,000 per month under a government nutrition scheme, as per Madhya Pradesh Economic Survey. The remaining did not receive a single instalment.
The Commission has observed that the contents of the news report, if true, raise serious issues of human rights violations. Therefore, it has issued a notice to the Chief Secretary, Government of Madhya Pradesh, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
According to the media report, carried on 26
th
November 2026, about 1.72 lakh cases of TB and 4,733 deaths were reported across the State in 2025.

content:
The National Human Rights Commission (NHRC), India has taken
suo motu
cognizance of a media report of 26th November 2026 that within a span of seven days, two prisoners died by suicide at two jails in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. Reportedly, an undertrial prisoner and another serving life imprisonment were found hanging at District Jail and Model Jail on 19th and 25th November 2026, respectively.

Therefore, it has issued notices to the Director General of Prisons, Uttar Pradesh and District Magistrate, Lucknow, calling for a detailed report on the matter within two weeks.
